goal: Verify that the entire pipeline works end-to-end: file upload → parsing → chunking → embedding → indexing in Weaviate. Document status must transition through each stage.
preconditions_global: You have a PDF file for testing (e.g. a drug leaflet, medical article — any PDF with text)

variables_legend.$PROJECT_ID: Project ID — copy from response of scenario 2.1
variables_legend.$DOCUMENT_ID: Document ID — copy from response of scenario 2.3
variables_legend.$PDF_PATH: Path to a PDF file on your machine, e.g. /Users/tomasz/Downloads/leaflet.pdf

scenarios.title: Create project with ingestion settings
scenarios.description: Before uploading you need a project. The project defines the chunking strategy, embedding provider and RAG mode. Testing project creation with full settings.

steps.action: Create a test project with default settings
steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/admin/projects -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"name": "Test Ingestion", "description": "Project for pipeline testing", "chunking_strategy": "recursive", "embedding_provider": "local_bge", "rag_mode": "vanilla"}' | python3 -m json.tool
steps.notes: Save the 'id' field as $PROJECT_ID — needed in every subsequent step

scenarios.expected_outcome: HTTP 201, project with id and settings

scenarios.title: Fetch project details
scenarios.description: Verify that the project is accessible and settings were saved correctly.

steps.action: Fetch project details by ID
steps.notes: Replace $PROJECT_ID with your id from step 2.1

scenarios.title: Upload PDF file — happy path
scenarios.description: Main ingestion test. PDF file is sent via multipart/form-data. The service saves the document in Mongo with status 'uploaded' and publishes an event to RabbitMQ. Response 202 Accepted = accepted for processing.
preconditions: You have a PDF file on disk

steps.action: Send PDF file via multipart/form-data
steps.notes: Replace $PDF_PATH with the file path, e.g. -F 'file=@/Users/tomasz/Downloads/test.pdf'. Status 202 Accepted means: received, processing asynchronously.

steps.action: Save document_id from response

scenarios.expected_outcome: HTTP 202, document with status=uploaded in MongoDB

scenarios.title: Upload — validation: unsupported file type (415 or 422)
scenarios.description: The system should reject files that are not PDF or DOCX.

steps.action: Try to upload a .txt file
steps.command: echo 'test content' > /tmp/test.txt && curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/ingest/projects/$PROJECT_ID/documents -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -F 'file=@/tmp/test.txt;type=text/plain' | python3 -m json.tool
steps.notes: Acceptable statuses: 415 Unsupported Media Type or 422 Unprocessable Entity

steps.action: Try to upload a .exe file (binary)
steps.command: echo -ne '\x4D\x5A' > /tmp/test.exe && curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/ingest/projects/$PROJECT_ID/documents -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -F 'file=@/tmp/test.exe;type=application/octet-stream' | python3 -m json.tool

scenarios.title: Upload — without token (401)
scenarios.description: The upload endpoint is protected. Without a token it must return 401.

steps.action: Send upload without Authorization header

scenarios.title: Upload — to non-existent project (404)
scenarios.description: Uploading to a project that does not exist should return 404, not 500.

steps.action: Send upload with a fake project_id
steps.notes: 000000000000000000000000 is a valid MongoDB ObjectId format but non-existent

scenarios.title: Deduplication — upload the same file twice
scenarios.description: The system computes a content_hash for each file. A second upload of the same file should not create a new document.
preconditions: Scenario 2.3 completed — file already uploaded once to $PROJECT_ID

steps.action: Send the same PDF file a second time

expected_response.detail: (duplicate message, e.g. 'Document with this content already exists')

steps.notes: If you get 202 again — content_hash deduplication is broken. Check ingestion service logs.

scenarios.title: Status tracking — check document status
scenarios.description: GET /ingest/projects/{pid}/documents/{did} returns the current document status and history of pipeline transitions.

steps.action: Check document status right after upload

expected_response.status: uploaded (or further if pipeline already started)

steps.notes: Status may already be 'parsing' or further if the pipeline is fast

scenarios.title: Pipeline E2E — tracking status transitions (polling)
scenarios.description: Document transitions through: uploaded → parsing → parsed → chunking → chunked → embedding → embedded → indexing → indexed. Track progress every few seconds.
preconditions: You have $PROJECT_ID and $DOCUMENT_ID, pipeline not yet finished

steps.action: Watch document status every 5 seconds (stop when status=indexed or failed)
steps.command: watch -n 5 "curl -s http://localhost:8000/ingest/projects/$PROJECT_ID/documents/$DOCUMENT_ID -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' | python3 -c 'import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(\"status:\", d.get(\"status\"), \"|\", len(d.get(\"status_history\", [])), \"steps\")'"
steps.expected_output:
Sequence of entries:
status: uploaded | 1 steps
status: parsing | 1 steps
status: parsed | 2 steps
status: chunking | 2 steps
...
status: indexed | 9 steps
steps.notes: Ctrl+C to stop watch. On macOS may need: brew install watch. Alternatively run curl manually every few seconds.

steps.action: Check final status and full history
steps.notes: status_history should contain at least 9 entries with timestamps and trace_id. If status=failed — check logs: docker compose logs parser chunking embedding indexing

scenarios.title: Pipeline diagnosis — what to do when status=failed
scenarios.description: If the document is stuck at some stage or has status 'failed', here is how to diagnose it.
preconditions: Document status is 'failed' or pipeline is stuck

steps.action: Check parser logs (parses PDF)
steps.expected_output: Look for: ERROR, Exception, Traceback. Common issues: 1) PDF is encrypted (pypdf cannot read it), 2) PDF contains only images (no text to extract)

steps.action: Check chunking logs
steps.expected_output: Look for: ERROR. Common issue: empty text from parser.

steps.action: Check embedding logs (slowest — loads ML model)
steps.expected_output: Look for: 'Loading model' (normal on startup), 'ERROR', 'CUDA out of memory' (GPU issue).
steps.notes: Embedding may take 30-120s on CPU depending on chunk count

steps.action: Check indexing logs (Weaviate)
steps.expected_output: Look for: 'ERROR', 'Connection refused' (Weaviate problem), 'schema not found'.

steps.action: Check for stuck messages in RabbitMQ
steps.command: curl -s -u guest:guest http://localhost:15672/api/queues | python3 -c "import sys,json; [print(f'{q[\"name\"]}: {q[\"messages\"]} msgs, {q[\"messages_unacknowledged\"]} unack') for q in json.load(sys.stdin)]"
steps.expected_output: A queue with messages > 0 and unack > 0 indicates a service that received the message but is not processing it

scenarios.expected_outcome: Root cause of the error found in logs

scenarios.title: Weaviate — verify chunks were indexed
scenarios.description: After the pipeline completes, the document's vectors should be in Weaviate. Verify chunk count and fields.

steps.action: Check that the Chunk class exists in Weaviate schema
steps.command: curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/schema | python3 -c "import sys,json; classes=[c['class'] for c in json.load(sys.stdin).get('classes',[])]; print('Classes:', classes)"
steps.notes: The Chunk class is created by the indexing service on the first ingest

steps.action: Count chunks in Weaviate
steps.command: curl -s 'http://localhost:8080/v1/objects?class=Chunk&limit=1' | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print('Total chunks:', d.get('totalResults', 'N/A'))"
steps.expected_output: Total chunks: (number > 0, e.g. 15 for a small PDF)
steps.notes: Number of chunks depends on PDF size and chunking strategy. For a 5-page PDF expect 10-30 chunks.

steps.action: Fetch a sample chunk and check its fields

objects.vector: (array of numbers — embedding, should be long, e.g. 768 or 1024 elements)

steps.notes: Key: the 'vector' field must be non-empty (these are the actual vectors). If vector=null — embedding did not work.

steps.action: Check chunks for a specific document via GraphQL
steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/graphql -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"query": "{ Get { Chunk(where: {path: [\"document_id\"], operator: Equal, valueText: \"$DOCUMENT_ID\"}) { content chunk_index document_id } } }"}' | python3 -m json.tool
steps.expected_output: List of chunks belonging to $DOCUMENT_ID with content and chunk_index fields
steps.notes: Replace $DOCUMENT_ID with your document id (without the $ sign). Chunks should be ordered by chunk_index.

scenarios.expected_outcome: Chunk class exists, chunks have non-empty vectors, chunks belong to $DOCUMENT_ID

scenarios.title: RabbitMQ — queues empty after pipeline completion
scenarios.description: After the pipeline finishes, all queues should be empty — every message was processed by its consumer.

steps.action: Check the state of all ingestion queues
steps.command: for queue in parser.queue chunking.queue embedding.queue indexing.queue; do echo -n "$queue: "; curl -s -u guest:guest "http://localhost:15672/api/queues/%2F/$queue" | python3 -c "import sys,json; q=json.load(sys.stdin); print(f'messages={q[\"messages\"]}, unack={q[\"messages_unacknowledged\"]}')"; done
steps.expected_output:
parser.queue: messages=0, unack=0
chunking.queue: messages=0, unack=0
embedding.queue: messages=0, unack=0
indexing.queue: messages=0, unack=0
steps.notes: If any queue has messages > 0 — the service did not process the message. Check its logs.

scenarios.title: Chunking — compare fixed_512 vs recursive strategies
scenarios.description: The system supports different chunking strategies. Create two projects with different strategies, upload the same PDF and compare chunk counts.
preconditions: You have $ADMIN_TOKEN and a PDF file

steps.action: Create project with fixed_512 strategy
steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/admin/projects -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"name": "Test fixed_512", "chunking_strategy": "fixed_512", "embedding_provider": "local_bge", "rag_mode": "vanilla"}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['id'])"

steps.action: Upload PDF to fixed_512 project and wait for indexed
steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8000/ingest/projects/$PROJECT_FIXED/documents -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' -F 'file=@$PDF_PATH' | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['id'])"

steps.action: Count chunks for fixed_512 project in Weaviate
steps.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/graphql -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d $'{"query": "{ Aggregate { Chunk(where: {path: [\"project_id\"], operator: Equal, valueText: \"$PROJECT_FIXED\"}) { meta { count } } } }"}' | python3 -m json.tool
steps.expected_output: Chunk count for the fixed_512 strategy
steps.notes: Compare with chunk count from the recursive project (2.1). fixed_512 creates fixed-length 512-token chunks — count may differ from recursive depending on the text.

scenarios.expected_outcome: Both projects have indexed chunks, their count differs between strategies

scenarios.title: Document status — non-existent document_id (404)
scenarios.description: GET status for a non-existent document should return 404.

steps.action: Fetch status of a non-existent document
